hok-east-drift-ice-road-trip.hook: Four days of sea ice, frozen lakes, wild swans and dancing cranes by 4WD.
moments: Stand on the deck of the Aurora icebreaker in Abashiri and hear sea ice crack under the hull.
Drive the Okhotsk coast to Utoro and watch the sea turn white near Oronko Rock at sunset.
Look down into frozen Lake Mashu from the 1st Observatory, a round blue-white bowl in the mountains.
Dig into the warm sand at Sunayu on Lake Kussharo while whooper swans float on the steaming water.
Watch red-crowned cranes call and dance in the snow at Tsurumidai before your Kushiro flight.
hok-east-drift-ice-road-trip.tip: Drive only in daylight, sunset is about 16:15. Book the first Aurora sailing: fewer people on the bow deck.

hok-asahikawa-sounkyo-abashiri.hook: Glowing ice towers, a hot onsen, then an icebreaker on the Okhotsk Sea.
moments: Drive east from Asahikawa into the Sounkyo gorge, with cliffs and frozen waterfalls beside the road.
Walk through lit ice tunnels and towers at the Ice Waterfall Festival, then soak in your hotel onsen.
Cross Sekihoku Pass in morning light, through white forest with almost no other cars.
Ride the Aurora icebreaker out of Abashiri for one hour, looking for sea ice and eagles.
hok-asahikawa-sounkyo-abashiri.tip: Leave Sounkyo early; the pass needs daylight. Check the Japan Coast Guard drift ice map the night before the cruise.

hok-shift-for-snow-festival.hook: Move nine days and Sapporo turns into a city of giant snow buildings.
moments: Walk the Odori Park blocks past five huge snow sculptures, some the size of real buildings.
Watch light shows projected onto the big snow sculptures after dark.
Walk the Susukino ice sculptures at night, with ramen and bars on every side.
Slide down long snow slides at the Tsudome site like kids.
Take a day trip to the Asahikawa Winter Festival and its giant snow stage.
hok-shift-for-snow-festival.tip: Go up the Sapporo TV Tower at the east end of Odori for the full view of the sculptures. Book hotels now.

hok-shikotsu-ice-festival.hook: Ice caves made of clear lake water, blue by day, rainbow-lit at night.
moments: Walk into ice caves and towers made by spraying Lake Shikotsu water onto frames until it freezes.
Look at the natural 'Shikotsu blue' of the ice in the afternoon light.
Stay as the colored lights switch on at 16:30 and the ice glows.
Listen to the ice creak in the cold, then warm up in a Shikotsu onsen nearby.
hok-shikotsu-ice-festival.tip: Arrive about 15:30 to see the blue ice and the lights in one visit. Monday Feb 1 costs ¥1,000, not ¥3,000.

hok-tomamu-ice-village.hook: Ski by day, then drink from a glass made of ice at night.
moments: Ride the gondola to the Frost Tree Terrace at 1,088 m and see trees coated in white frost.
Ski Tomamu's wide groomed runs: fast ones for the good skier, easy ones for the beginner.
Walk the Ice Village at night: ice dome hotel, ice chapel, ice rink with light projections.
Drink at the Ice Bar from an ice glass, then ride the ice slide down.
Eat ice cheese fondue or the 'iceberg' bouillabaisse at the Ice Restaurant.
hok-tomamu-ice-village.tip: Go up to the Frost Tree Terrace early on a cold, clear morning; the frost on the trees melts later in the day.

hok-sounkyo-ice-waterfall.hook: Walk through glowing ice tunnels in a gorge, then soak in hot spring water.
moments: Enter the festival site by the river and walk under tall ice towers lit in blue, green and red.
Go through the ice tunnels and visit the small ice shrine.
Feel the gorge air at about -15°C while your breath freezes on your scarf.
Walk back to your hotel and soak in the onsen with snow falling outside.
hok-sounkyo-ice-waterfall.tip: Stay the night in Sounkyo so you can visit late, after 20:00, when the crowds are small. Wear shoes with grip.

hok-garinko-mombetsu.hook: A ship with two giant screw drills that grinds its way through sea ice.
moments: Board Garinko III IMERU at Mombetsu port and walk to the bow deck.
Watch the two red screw drills at the front roll onto the ice and crush it.
Hear the grinding and cracking as white ice plates split into blue sea water.
Visit the Okhotsk Tower after the cruise, an observatory that stands out in the sea.
hok-garinko-mombetsu.tip: Book when 2027 reservations open on Oct 9, 2026. Stand at the bow rail early; it is the best spot to see the drills.

hok-toya-noboribetsu.hook: A volcano lake onsen, then a steaming valley that smells of sulfur.
moments: Soak in a lakeside onsen at Toya and look out at the dark water and snowy Showa-Shinzan volcano.
Watch the short winter fireworks over Lake Toya from your room, if they run in 2027.
Walk the boardwalk through Jigokudani 'Hell Valley', with steam vents and the smell of sulfur all around.
See the red oni demon statues around Noboribetsu town and the Enma statue at Enmado.
Try many baths from different hot springs in one big Noboribetsu onsen hotel.
hok-toya-noboribetsu.tip: Walk Jigokudani early in the morning; in the cold the steam is thicker and the path is empty. Bring shoe spikes.

hok-other-ski-areas.hook: Deep January powder at four resorts, each with easy runs for beginners.
moments: Ride through the trees at Rusutsu, with three mountains and far fewer people than Niseko.
Ski the deep, soft snow at Kiroro, one of the snowiest resorts in Hokkaido.
Ski down Sapporo Teine's Olympic runs with the sea and Sapporo city below you.
Take the Furano ropeway up and look out over the snowy Tokachi mountains.
hok-other-ski-areas.tip: Book a half-day ski school lesson for the beginner in the morning; the good skier explores, then meet for lunch.

hok-otaru-tenguyama-yoichi.hook: Whisky made over coal fires, then Otaru harbor lights from a mountain top.
moments: Walk the red-roof stone buildings of Nikka Yoichi, the first Nikka distillery, from 1934.
Watch the pot stills heated by coal fire, the same old method founder Taketsuru learned in Scotland.
See Taketsuru's old house, then taste the free Nikka samples at the end of the tour.
Ride the Tenguyama ropeway at dusk and rub the tengu's long nose for luck.
Look down at Otaru harbor lights, one of Hokkaido's three famous night views.
hok-otaru-tenguyama-yoichi.tip: Book the Nikka tour online about one month before; there is no same-day entry. The driver gets soft drinks.

hok-sapporo-city-day.hook: Snowy shrine, beer in red brick, and miso ramen: three Sapporo classics.
moments: Walk through Maruyama Park's snowy forest to Hokkaido Jingu and its quiet wooden shrine.
Eat a warm grilled mochi 'Hangan-sama' at the teahouse inside the shrine grounds.
Taste beer in the red-brick Sapporo Beer Museum, including a beer you can only drink there.
Grill Genghis Khan lamb on a dome-shaped iron pan at the Sapporo Beer Garden next door.
End in Ganso Ramen Yokocho in Susukino with a bowl of rich miso ramen with butter and corn.
hok-sapporo-city-day.tip: Book a Beer Garden table for early dinner, then walk off the lamb before ramen. Your clothes will smell of lamb.

hok-jozankei-onsen.hook: Sapporo's onsen town in a snowy river valley, one hour from the city.
moments: Take the bus from Sapporo into the deep valley as the snow gets thicker.
Walk the river path to the red Futami suspension bridge over a steaming stream.
Look for the green kappa water-spirit statues all around town.
Soak your feet in the free public foot bath, then soak in your hotel's river-view open-air bath.
hok-jozankei-onsen.tip: Book the Kappa Liner bus from Sapporo. Get a room with dinner included; the town has few restaurants at night.

hok-kamui-misaki.hook: A thin rocky cape over a very blue sea, but mostly a summer place.
moments: Drive the Shakotan coast road from Otaru past fishing villages and dark cliffs.
Walk through the old gate at the start of the 770 m ridge path, if the wind lets it open.
Look down at the rocks and the cold winter sea from the path.
hok-kamui-misaki.tip: In late January the path often closes for wind. Go on a calm day, or skip it and spend the time in Otaru.

hok-akan-ainu-cranes.hook: Ainu songs by a frozen lake, then wild cranes dancing in the snow.
moments: Walk the Akan Ainu Kotan street, full of carved wood shops, in a village of about 120 Ainu people.
Watch 'Lost Kamuy' at the Ainu Theater Ikor, a show with Ainu dance and digital images.
Walk out onto frozen Lake Akan and, in festival time, watch fireworks over the ice.
Watch wild red-crowned cranes call and dance in the snowy field at Tsurumidai.
Stand on Otowa Bridge at dawn to see cranes in the river mist on very cold mornings.
hok-akan-ainu-cranes.tip: For Otowa Bridge, arrive before sunrise on a day below -15°C; the river steam and frost are strongest then.
